title: ALMA detection of 321 GHz water maser emission in the radio galaxy NGC 1052
question: Is there 321 GHz H2O maser emission in the radio galaxy NGC 1052, and how do its profile and location compare with the known 22 GHz maser?

what.value: Absorption-line spectra (H2O 5(5,0)-6(4,3) v2=1, HCN 1-0 and 4-3) overplotted in Figure 1

evidence.quote: together with absorption lines of H$_2$O $5_{5,0}-6_{4,3}$, $v_2=1$, HCN $1-0$, and $4-3$ (cite: 2020ApJ...895...73K; 2023ApJsubmitted)

what.value: Continuum brightness temperature of NGC 1052 exceeding 1e8 K

evidence.quote: Since the brightness temperature of the continuum emission exceeds $10^8$ K (cite: 2004A&A...426..481K)

what.value: Maser excitation condition: 321-GHz maser needs T_k > 1000 K and n(H2O) > 1e4 cm^-3

evidence.quote: calculated the excitation condition of possible H$_2$O maser transitions for evolved star environments

what.value: 321 GHz maser properties of Circinus galaxy and NGC 4945 used for comparison (peak-to-continuum ratios 3.2 and 37 for Circinus, 0.29 for NGC 4945)

evidence.loc: 3.3 Comparison with the Circinus galaxy and NGC 4945
evidence.quote: In this subsection we compare the properties of the H$_2$O maser in NGC 1052 with those in NGC 4945 and the Circinus galaxy referring to

evidence.loc: 3.3 Comparison with the Circinus galaxy and NGC 4945
evidence.quote: The ratio in NGC 4945 was 0.29 on 2012-06-03 and there was a non detection on 2017-05-06.

what.value: SO absorption temperatures 26 +/- 4 K (mm) and 344 +/- 43 K (sub-mm)

evidence.loc: 3.2 Spectral profiles and location of masers
evidence.quote: found mm (86 – 130 GHz) molecular absorption features and identified different line profiles from sub-mm ones

recipe.method: Standard spectral calibration in GBTIDL; spectra at 0.33 km/s resolution for six epochs
key_parameters: rms per epoch 2.3, 2.7, 2.1, 1.4, 4.6, 2.5 mJy; ~10% systematic flux error

recipe.goal: extract and fit the 321 GHz line profile
recipe.method: Continuum-subtracted ALMA spectrum fitted with two Gaussian components (broad and narrow)
key_parameters: Broad: centre 1467 +/- 5 km/s, FWHM 208 +/- 12 km/s; narrow: centre 1333 +/- 1 km/s, FWHM 44 +/- 3 km/s

recipe.goal: locate the maser emission relative to the continuum
recipe.method: Channel maps in 20 km/s slices over 1280-1580 km/s; position measured by 2-D Gaussian fitting in each channel map and registered on the continuum image

recipe.goal: constrain source sizes from the uv plane
recipe.method: uv-plot analysis of continuum and continuum-subtracted velocity-integrated line emission giving 99% confidence upper limits on FWHM size

recipe.goal: test thermal versus maser origin via brightness temperature
recipe.method: Brightness temperature lower limit from size upper limit and peak flux density, plus ancillary arguments (absorption against the core, compactness vs CND)
assumptions: Thermal molecular gas covering the bright continuum core would appear in absorption

recipe.goal: derive isotropic maser luminosities and compare with Circinus and NGC 4945
recipe.method: Isotropic luminosity L = 1.04e-3 nu_rest D_L^2 integral S(v) dv for 22 and 321 GHz masers; compare peak-to-continuum ratios

evidence.quote: the isotropic luminosity of 1090 $L_{\Sol}$.

evidence.loc: 3.3 Comparison with the Circinus galaxy and NGC 4945

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA calibration and imaging parameters are not given in the paper (see unstated_but_needed); must be taken from the GitHub scripts

Two-Gaussian fit and uv-plane size-limit procedures are not described in detail
score_reason: ALMA project code, observing date, spectral setup, beam, rms and all main numbers are given, and reduction scripts plus reduced data are on GitHub; but calibration, imaging and fitting settings are only in the repository, not in the paper.
rediscovery_reason: Single ALMA project (2021.1.00341.S, observed 2022-05-12) with scripts on GitHub and numeric line parameters (FWHM, centre velocities, luminosity) that can be re-derived; public availability of the ALMA data is not stated in the paper and is assumed from the archive link.
